status.en: 17 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 26% fewer than the week before, most of them in La Espriella, Espriella and Bogota.
status.nb: 17 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 26 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i La Espriella, Espriella og Bogota.

summary.en: The Indigenous Guard in Colombia has taken up arms against the new president's agenda, while President De la Espriella ordered a fifth bombing that killed nine ELN members. Ecuadorian authorities arrested four FARC dissident leaders on the border, linking cross-border rebel activity to the Colombian conflict. A drone strike injured six police officers at a Colombian police station, and a Black Hawk crash left thirteen soldiers stranded in Cauca. An illegal gold mine collapse in southwestern Colombia killed fourteen miners and injured seven, adding a civilian disaster to the ongoing armed violence.
summary.nb: Den urfolksgarden i Colombia har tatt opp våpen mot den nye presidentens agenda, mens president De la Espriella beordret en femte bombe som drepte ni ELN-medlemmer. Ekvatorske myndigheter arresterte fire FARC-dissidentledere ved grensen, og knyttet grenseoverskridende opprørsaktivitet til den colombianske konflikten. Et droneangrep påførte seks politifolk skader på en colombiansk politistasjon, og en Black Hawk-ulykke etterlot tretten soldater strandet i Cauca. Et ulovlig gullgruvekollaps i sør-vestlige Colombia drepte fjorten gruvearbeidere og såret sju, og la til en sivil katastrofe i den pågående væpnede volden.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
